resources.title: Comprehension #1
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 4 | Content: Reading Class appropriate informational texts e.g. texts on diet and nutrition, benefits of eating for healthy living, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. read class appropriate informational texts e.g. health, environment, consumer rights, safety etc.; 2. identify main ideas in the texts; and 3. identify supporting facts in the texts
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to read the story. 2. Guides pupils to identify main ideas in the texts 3. Guides pupils to identify supporting facts in a text.

Students: 1. Read the informational texts. 2. Work in pairs or groups to identify main ideas in the texts. 3. Work in pairs or groups to identify main facts in the texts
resources.resources: 1. Newspapers, magazines 2. Course book 3. Supplementary readers 4. Pictures
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. read the the informational texts; 2. discuss the main ideas in the texts; and 3. list the main facts in the read texts

resources.title: Comprehension #2
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 4 | Content: Reading Class appropriate stories and poems to: - identify words, similes and metaphors, - explain the characters, setting and plots in poems and stories.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. read class appropriate stories and poems with understanding; 2. answer questions on the poems and stories; 3. identify and interpret similes and metaphors; and 4. understand characters, setting plots.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to read selected stories and poems. 2. Explains similarities and differences between simple stories (prose) and poems. 4. Asks and guides pupils to answer questions. 5. Explains the language of poetry to pupils e.g. rhymes and rhythm, etc. 6. Guides the pupils to identify similes and metaphors in poems

Students: 1. Read stories and poems. 2. Discuss similarities and differences they observed in stories (prose) and poems with the teacher‟s guidance. 3. Answer questions individually, in pairs or in groups. 4. identify similes and metaphors in poems
resources.resources: 1. Selected stories and poems 2. Course books 3. Flash cards 4. pictures and drawings 5. Real objects 6. Supplementary reading materials
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Read stories and poems; 2. list 3 features of poems; 3. mention at least 3 examples of similes and metaphors; and 4. explain the meaning of character and setting plot

resources.title: Comprehension #3
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 4 | Content: Independent reading: - Reading independently for a purpose; - Independent selection of books and other reading materials.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. set purpose for reading; 2. read story books and other reading materials independently for entertainment, enjoyment or information; and 3. select books and other reading materials independently
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to read story books, supplementary readers, etc independently 2. Guides the pupils to understand the purpose of independent reading 3. Helps pupils to develop reading habits. 4. Guides pupils on how to select books and other reading materials 5. Guides pupils to summarize what they have read

Students: Pupils to: 1. Read story books and other reading materials independently 2. Recognize the purpose of reading any text 3. Show interest in reading independently 4. Select books and other reading materials on their own 5. Pupils to summarize what they have read
resources.resources: 1. Story books 2. Supplementary Readers 3. Charts on how to select books in the library 4. Newspaper, magazines etc
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. read story books and other reading materials; 2. mention at least 3 purposes of reading different texts; 3. explain how to select books and other reading materials; and 4. summarize at least one book read

resources.title: Concepts of print
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 4 | Content: 1. Recognizing charts, maps, graphs, pictures, etc. in printed materials and texts 2. Parts of text e.g. title, title page, table of content, glossary, index etc. 3. Previewing text using text features.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify different types of fonts, illustrations, graphics etc; 2. use title, title page, table of content, glossary and index to locate information; preview text using text features e.g. headings, graphics, titles, diagram, etc; and 3. recognize different kinds of text- poems, plays, drama, letters, biographies etc.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Guides pupils to recognize and use charts, maps, graphs, pictures etc. 2. Guides pupils to identify parts of texts e.g. title of text, title page, table of content, glossary, index etc. 3. Guides pupils to locate information in texts using parts of text. 4. Guides pupils to preview a text using headings, graphics, titles etc.

Students: Pupils to: 1. Recognize and use charts, maps, graphs, pictures etc. 2. Identify parts of text e.g. title of text, table of content, glossary, etc. 3. Locate information in text using parts of text 4. Preview texts using text features e.g. headings, graphics, titles etc.
resources.resources: 1. Recommended books 2. supplementary readers 3. Story books
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Recognize and use maps, graphs, pictures, etc; 2. Identify parts of texts; 3. Locate information from texts using parts of text; and 4. Preview a text using text features.

resources.title: Writing Simple Sentences about Events in Correct Sequence. (A Passage on Consumer, Market and Society)
resources.description: Theme: WRITING PRIMARY 4 | Content: 1. Meaning of consumer, market and society. 2. Key operators in the market e.g. consumers, goods and service providers, government, etc. 3. Impact of market on society.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. explain who a consumer is using simple sentences; 2. explain the meaning of a market; 3. list three key market operators in simple sentences; and 4. in simple sentences, discuss the roles of market in the society.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of consumer, market and society in simple sentences e.g. „A consumer buys goods and services‟. 2. Discusses the impact of market on society using simple sentences. 3. Takes learners on a trip to a market.

Students: Participate in explanation of consumer, market and society in simple sentences.
resources.resources: 1. Posters, charts, fliers showing market scenes. 2. Magazines, pictures, newspapers, cutting of relevant information on consumer and society. 3. Textbooks.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. explain the meaning of consumer, market and society; 2. list three key market operators; and 3. give two impacts of market on society.

resources.title: Guided Informal Letter, e.g. Letter to a Friend
resources.description: Theme: WRITING PRIMARY 4 | Content: 1. An informal letter. E.g. A letter to an elder sister, a brother, a father, a mother, a friend. 2. Features of informal letter: Letter to a friend is based on: tolerance, humaneness, personal in tone, intimate with secret/gossip, to share and enjoy warmth.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. make appropriate use of guidelines to write an informal letter; and 2. write an informal letters.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Teacher explains meaning of informal letter. 2. Lists the formal features of an inform letter. 3. Guides pupils to write informal letters.

Students: 1. Listen to and write down in their books meaning of, and features of informal letters. 2. Write informal letters to relatives and friends. 3. Participate in class discussions.
resources.resources: 1. A suitable guided informal letter formats. 2. An informal letter prepared by the teacher.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. use the guidelines correctly to write an informal letter; and 2. write informal letter correctly.

resources.title: Narrative and Descriptive Composition Descriptive: 1. My Family 2. My School
resources.description: Theme: WRITING RIMARY 4 | Content: 1. Describe piece of writing, bringing out important events or highlight. 2. Communicate these thoughts in a continuous prose. 3. Get, through the help of pupils, the different exciting events in their lives. 4. Describing the members of the family (including pets) 5. Describing a typical day in the life of the family.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. narrate a story; 2. write a composition on a given topic; 3. describe the essential characteristics of their family or school; and 4. describe the members of the family, noting their special characters
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Prepares model compositions on narrative and descriptive and use these to guide pupils. 2. Discusses the content of the composition with pupils; each mentioning their own memorable days. 3. Let‟s them say why it is memorable. 4. Let them write it as a creative piece of writing to be displayed on the notice board.

Students: 1. Write compositions (narrative and descriptive) given by the teacher. 2. Copy the model compositions given by the teacher. 3. Talk about their experiences with regard to the events. 4. Read over the work on the chalkboard. 5. Write two or three paragraphs on their own memorable day.
resources.resources: 1. Picture charts of exciting events. 2. Model narrative and descriptive passages. 3. Course book. 4. Composition prepared by the teacher. 5. Supplementary reader.
resources.assessment: 1. Pupils to narrative their own story; 2. Write their own composition on a topic of their interest; 3. Describe their family or school environment; and 4. Describe members of their family noting their special characters.

resources.title: Simple Conversation using the Appropriate Words
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 4 | Content: 1. Practice in excusing, obligation, permission etc 2. „can‟ meaning possible 3. „must‟ meaning obligation „ought to‟ meaning what is right.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. engage in simple conversation involving, excuse, obligation, permission etc; 2. use modal auxiliaries to make sentences such as: „can i come in‟?; and 3. use modal auxiliaries in sentences in contextual situations so as to bring out their meaning.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. List the modal auxiliaries 2. Creates short stories around the family using modal auxiliaries 3. Asks questions on the story e.g. can Adamu wash the plate? 4. Constructs a dialogue for the same purpose 5. Guides the pupils to dialogue in pairs emphasizing on the modal auxiliaries.

Students: 1. Make sentences after teacher‟s modal examples with „can‟, „cannot‟, „may‟, „may not‟, „must‟, „must not‟, „ought to‟, „ought not to‟, etc. 2. Create a short scene where the pupils role play and use auxiliaries in their conversation 3. Make sentences on their own with modal auxiliaries.
resources.resources: 1. Real objects 2. Approved course book 3. Pictures showing actions of the conversatio ns
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. use each of the modal auxiliaries correctly; and 2. say short sentences using auxiliaries.

resources.title: Aural Discrimination in Vowels and Consonants
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 4 | Content: 1 Discriminate between the sounds /˄/ and /3:/ cup curb luck lurk gull girl bust burst 1. Aural consonants as chop/shop, catch/cash, very/ ferry, have/half 2. Distinguishes the pair of voiced and voiceless consonant sounds.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1 distinguish between the sounds /˄/ in bud and sound /3:/ in bird /a/ in bag and /a:/ in bark; 2 recognize the sounds in words; 3 draw the contrast between sounds when they use the words; and 4 discriminate between two pairs of consonants e.g. /t/Ϛ/ chin /Ϛ/ shin /v/ vest /f/ first.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1 Writes out the words and the sounds symbols 2 Pronounce the sounds 3 Drills the pupils on the sound distinctions in the words 4 Writes and pronounce vowels and consonant sounds in the word contexts.

Students: 1 Practice the new vowel and consonant sounds and in word context 2 Write the words and the sound symbols in their note books 3 Differentiate the voiced and voiceless consonants.
resources.resources: 1 Course book 2 Any suitable book on English phonetics 3 Tape recorder with speech cassettes.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1 do oral drills; 2 recognize the sound; 3 contrast the two vowel sounds; and 4 distinguish between two pairs of consonant words.

resources.title: Oral Composition Descriptive and Narrative e.g. - An Interesting experience : “A visit to my village‟” - “„My Father‟s house”.
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 4 | Content: 1. Narrating an interesting experience with the following: - „A visit to my village‟, „My first day in school‟ 2. Describing places or how things are done e.g. „My school‟, „How to cook rice‟.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. narrate the highlights of „a visit to my village‟; 2. narrate a story; 3. describe how things are been done or a place, e.g. „my father‟s house‟; and 4. pick out important features in any event with emphasis on time, place, occasion and significance.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads discussions dramatization based on „A visit to my village‟ or an interesting experience in „ my school‟ or any descriptive topic 2. Organizes out of class activities to visit places of interest and asks the pupils to narrate or describe their experiences.

Students: 1. Narrate some events they witnessed 2. Participate actively in teacher initiated activities 3. Describe their memorable days individually.
resources.resources: 1. Text books showing various events 2. Video clips of events 3. Real objects to describe how things are done.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. describe some events accurately; and 2. narrate interesting experiences they have witnessed.

resources.title: Using Question Tags
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 4 | Content: 1. Positive Tomorrow is Monday, isn’t it? You are a boy/girl, Aren’t you? She is quite attractive, isn’t she? We shall see each other again, shan’t we? 2. Negative: You didn’t come to school, did you? This book isn’t yours, is it?
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Ask and respond to question tags; 2. Making sentences adding question tags; and 3. Use tags in asking question either positive or negative
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Lets pupils use tags correctly as in content columns 2. Engages the pupils in various conversations involving positive and negative tags 3. Guides pupils to generate questions using tags 4. Shows the pupils questions and what tags to be used i.e. positive tag or negative.

Students: 1. Listen attentively to the teacher and ask questions using tags 2. In pairs, they engage in conversation using correct questions with correct tags 3. Identify what tags to be used for various questions.
resources.resources: 1. Course book 2. Teacher‟s guide 3. Other relevant materials.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. use tags correctly in questions; and 2. make sentences adding the question tags.

resources.title: Stress and Intonation
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 4 | Content: 1. Stress pattern can be represented as: / stressed; \unstressed e.g. / WRIting it now / SEnd it now /BEAutiful girl 2. Intonation and stress change the meaning of sentence, e.g. You want me to stay (statement) You want me to stay? (Question).
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1 utter each expression with the correct stress; 2 use intonation pattern to express meaning; and 3. distinguish the contrast between the two expressions both in statement and in question.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Expresses the stress pattern e.g. „writing‟ has only one stress „wri‟ 2. Says the expression once and lets pupils say after him/her three times 3. Guides the pupils to point out differences in meaning 4. Provides sentences and pronounce them in the appropriate intonation and stress pattern.

Students: 1. Say each phrases expressing correct stress 2. Use pronunciation pattern provided by the teacher in sentences to show stress and intonation 3. Answer questions on stress and intonation.
resources.resources: 1. Course book 2. Any practical book on phonetics.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. do oral drill; 2. make correct sentences with correct stress and intonation; and 3. do oral exercise.

resources.title: Songs and Poems
resources.description: Theme: LISTENING AND SPEAKING PRIMARY 4 | Content: 1. Read and sing. 2. Poems and songs. Discuss the theme of poem (subject matter and meaning). 3. Songs as another useful instrument of speech training and memorization.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. read and sing poems and songs as instruments of speech training; 2. memorize and recite poems; 3. sing and enjoy the song; 4. discuss meaning and effect of poem; and 5. identify the theme of poem.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Leads pupils to study the poem. 2. Reads poems to pupils to arouse interest. 3. Lets pupils take turns reading the poem. 4. Reads the song as a poem. 5. Lets the pupils read after him/her. 6. Encourages them to memorize the songs. 7. Teaches the pupils to sing the song and enjoy it.

Students: 1. Listen to the teacher read the poem and sing song. 2. Take turns in reading the poem and singing the songs. 3. Memorize the poem and the song. 4. Read the poem in group chorally and individually. 5. Read the poem and sing the song to get details of the meaning. 6. Learn to sing and enjoy the song.
resources.resources: 1. A short poem on a cardboard. 2. Flash cards showing key words in the poem and songs. 3. Simple poetry books 4. Other relevant materials. 5. Charts containing the song. 6. Course book.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. Read the song as a poem; 2. memorize and recite it correctly; 3. discuss the meaning and effect of the poem; 4. identify the theme of the poem; and 5. memorize the song, song and enjoy it.

resources.title: Using past, present and future tenses accurately
resources.description: Theme: GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY PRIMARY 4 | Content: 1. Past tense e.g. I ate yesterday 2. Present tense e.g. I eat rice everyday 3. Future tense e.g. I will eat salad tomorrow.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Correctly use: (a) past tense (b) present tense (c) Future tense.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the use of past, present and future tenses. 2. Guides pupils to use the past, present and future tenses.

Students: 1. Identify past, present and future tenses. 2. Use past, present and future sentences in making statements/se ntences.
resources.resources: 1.Course book 2. Substitutio n tables
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify past, present and future tenses; and 2. make correct use of past, present and future tenses.

resources.title: Nouns and pronouns
resources.description: Theme: GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY PRIMARY 4 | Content: - Identification of nouns and pronouns - Use of nouns and pronouns.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify nouns and pronouns; and 2. use nouns and pronouns in making sentences.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains nouns and pronouns. 2. Guides pupils to identify nouns and pronouns. 3. Guides pupils to use nouns and pronouns in sentences.

Students: 1. Identify nouns and pronouns 2. Use nouns and pronouns in making sentences.
resources.resources: 1. Course book 2. Real objects 3. Pictures
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify nouns and pronouns in statements/ sentences; and 2. construct five sentences using nouns and pronouns.

resources.title: Adjectives and Adverbs
resources.description: Theme: GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY PRIMARY 4 | Content: - Identification of adjectives and adverbs - Use of adjectives and adverbs.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. identify adjectives and adverbs; and 2. use adjectives and adverbs in making sentences.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains adjectives and adverbs. 2. Guides pupils to identify adjectives and adverbs. 3. Guides pupils to use adjectives and adverbs in making sentences.

Students: 1. Identify adjectives and adverbs 2. Use adjectives and adverbs in making sentences.
resources.resources: 1. Course book 2. Real objects 3. Pictures
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify adjectives and adverbs in statements/ sentences; and 2. make correct use of adjectives and adverbs.

resources.title: Comparative forms of adjectives and adverbs
resources.description: Theme: GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY PRIMARY 4 | Content: 1. Comparative forms of adjectives e.g. He is taller than his father; Bimpe is more intelligent than Ayo 2. Comparative forms of adverbs e.g. Ahmed walks more slowly than Eze.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to use the comparative forms of adjectives and adverbs correctly.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Gives examples of the comparative forms of adjectives and adverbs. 2. Guides pupils to use the comparative forms of adjectives and adverbs.

Students: 1. Identify the comparative forms of adjectives and adverbs. 2. Use comparative forms in sentences.
resources.resources: 1. Course book 2. Charts containing comparative and superlative
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify the comparative forms of adjectives and adverbs; 2. use comparative forms in sentences.

resources.title: Question Tags
resources.description: Theme: GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY PRIMARY 4 | Content: 1. Question tags when body of sentence is positive and the tail is negative e.g. she is beautiful, isn‟t she? Today is Wednesday, isn‟t it? 2. Question tags when the body is negative and the tail is positive e.g. she will not come, will she? You did not fail, did you?
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. ask and respond to question tags; 2. make sentences, adding the question tags; and 3. use the negative and positive tags correctly.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1.Explains when to use question tags 2. Gives examples and asks pupils to repeat after him/her. 3. Guides pupils to use question tags.

Students: 1. Make sentences that involve question tags. 2. Do oral drills on negative question tags.
resources.resources: 1. Substitution table 2. Course book 3. Flash card
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. ask and respond to question tags correctly; 2. make sentences, adding the question tags correctly; and 3. Use the positive and negative tags correctly.

resources.title: Adverbial Clauses using „if‟ and „when‟
resources.description: Theme: GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY PRIMARY 4 | Content: - Adverbial clause of condition (if) e.g. If we know our rights as Nigerians, nobody can abuse them; - Adverbial clause of condition (when) e.g. When we pay our taxes, the government will do more for the citizens.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. use adverbial clause of condition (if) correctly; and 2. use adverbial clause of condition (when) correctly.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1.Explains adverbial clauses of condition using “if” and “when” 2. Guides pupils to use adverbial clauses in making sentences.

Students: 1. Identify target adverbial clauses. 2. Use of adverbial clauses of condition “if” and “when”.
resources.resources: 1. Course book 2. Flash cards 3. Picture
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. identify adverbial clause of condition “if” and “when”; and 2. Make correct use of clause of condition “if” and “when”.

resources.title: Phonics #1
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 5 | Content: Intonation patterns in statements, questions commands and requests e.g. „Is he coming?‟ (Falling, Rising Intonation) „Will you read the book very fast?‟ (falling, rising, rising, rising)
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. use the intonation required in statements, questions commands and requests; correctly; and 2. use stress correctly to convey meaning.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Introduces the lesson by showing the charts containing these sentences to pupils and guiding them to read the sentences. 2. Supervises pupils‟ practice and use of the appropriate intonation.

Students: 1. Repeat the sentences after the teacher, using the intonation pattern provided by him/her e.g. “Will you do the sums accurately?” 2. Practice the falling/rising intonation pattern typical of a statement, question, command and a request.
resources.resources: 1. Course book 2. Books on sounds, stress and intonation of English. 3. A chart of some sentences differently stressed 4. Audio-player
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. use the appropriate stress and intonation in giving commands and requests; and 2. use stress and intonation in dialogues to demonstrate questioning.

resources.title: Phonics #2
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 5 | Content: More on Aural Discrimination: Vowels, Consonants, Diphthongs, digraphs and trigraphs.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1.produce the sounds of each word correctly; 2.recognise the sounds; 3.draw the contrast between sounds when used in words; and 4. use each word in correct sentence.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Produces the pairs of sounds which contrast and lets pupils repeat after him. e.g: /ӕ/ and /a: /,as in „cat‟ and „cart‟, „pat‟ and „part‟ /˄/and /Ͻ:/ as in „one‟ and ‟warn‟ /p/ and /f/ as in „pill‟ and „fill‟, /ᶴ/ and/tᶴ/ as in „shop‟ and „chop‟ etc. 2. Writes the words containing the sounds in minimal pairs on the chalk board. 3. Guides pupils to produce the sounds in isolation and in words. 4. Guides pupils to construct sentences with each pair and bring out the contrast.

Students: 1. Repeat the pairs of sounds produced by the teacher in isolation and in words 2. Construct sentences with each pair to bring out the contrast.
resources.resources: 1.Course book 2.Charts containing the minimal pair 3.Speech cassettes 4. Any other suitable material on phonetics
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1.distinguish between three pairs of sounds; 2.recognize the sounds; 3.draw the contrast between three pairs of sounds when used in words; and 4.use the three pairs of words in sentences to bring out their meanings

resources.title: Comprehension #1
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 5 | Content: Reading from content specific materials e.g. relevant passages on road safety, health, consumer rights, etc.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. read content specific materials e.g. on health, consumer education and other kinds of information, 2. Identify main ideas in materials read, 3. Identify and summarise supporting details.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Selects and presents appropriate passages e.g. health, road safety, consumer rights. 2. Explains relevant unfamiliar words 3. Explains to pupils how to read these passages and obtain information. 4. Guides pupils to read passages and answer questions.

Students: 1. Examine materials presented by teacher. 2. Read passages. 3. Identify and use new words in sentences. 4.Answer questions based on passages.
resources.resources: 1. Passages from relevant materials e.g. Road Safety Guide. 2. Materials from other sources.
resources.assessment: Pupils to read passages to get relevant information.

resources.title: Comprehension #2
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 5 | Content: Reading non-fiction passages to: 1. identify main ideas, sequence of events, characters, plot, setting, etc. 2. discuss similarities and differences, 3. summarise and draw conclusions.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. read non-fiction passages; and 2. identify and discuss main ideas in non-fiction passages.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains the meaning of non- fiction and differentiates it from fiction. 2. Presents a selected non-fiction passage reflecting important national values or issues, e.g. unity, security. 3. Guides pupils to read passage. 4. Guides pupils to identify and discuss main ideas in the passage.

Students: 1. Read the given passage silently. 2. Work in pairs or groups to identify main ideas in particular paragraphs. 3. Participate in plenary presentation/disc ussion of group work.
resources.resources: 1. Selected non- fiction passages from various sources 2. Course books 3. Flip charts/card board papers 4. Chalk board/
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. read a given passage fluently and at the right speed; and 2. identify main ideas in a given non-fiction passage.

resources.title: Comprehension #3
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 5 | Content: Reading and answering questions from Class Appropriate texts and Poems
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. read simple selected children‟s novels and poems; 2. answer factual and other questions from selected children‟s novels and poems, 3. identify similes and metaphor.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Explains to pupils why they need to read. 2. Exposes pupils to different kinds of children‟s novels and poetry collections. 3. Guides the pupils to read simple children‟s novels and poems. 4. Guides pupils to identify and discuss good reading habits. 5. Guides pupils to answer factual questions from the selected novels and poems.

Students: 1. Set daily/weekly targets for reading children‟s novels and poems. 2. Acquire good reading habits. 3. Answer questions from teacher and other pupils.
resources.resources: 1. Course book 2. Supplementary readers 3. Books from the library (children‟s novels and poetry collections)
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. keep a record of books read; 2. answer questions based on books and poetry collections read; and 3. identify good reading habits.

resources.title: Comprehension #4
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 5 | Content: Reading for Implied Meaning: - Reading relevant passages on national social service institutions, e.g. CPC, FRSC, ICPC, NAFDAC, NDLEA, NEMA
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to read passages and draw out meanings from information that is not expressly stated in the text.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Selects relevant passages that illustrate the concept of implied meaning. 2. Explains to pupils what is meant by implied meaning. 3. Guides pupils to read the passage. 4. Guides pupils to use context and other methods to draw out implied meanings from the passage. 5. Guides pupils to answer questions.

Students: 1. Follow teacher‟s explanations 2. Read passage silently. 3. Work in pairs or in groups to get implied meanings to the passages. 4. Discuss ideas from the passage. 5. Answer questions on passages.
resources.resources: 1. Selected passages. 2. Course book. 3. Flip charts/ card boards 4. Chalk/white board
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. read a given passage; 2. answer relevant questions on the passage; and 3. draw out implied meaning from the passage.

resources.title: Vocabulary
resources.description: Theme: READING PRIMARY 5 | Content: Reading for vocabulary development: - Reading relevant passages on marriage, family, health, sports, safety (registers).
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. read and use context clues from a passage to determine the meaning of unfamiliar words, 2. use common spelling patterns to determine the meaning of new words.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Selects passages that contain the new words that children need to learn. 2. Makes a list of new words and explains their meanings and uses. 3. Guides children to discuss the new words and their uses.

Students: 1. Read the given passages. 2. Identify and discuss new words. 3. Use new words in making sentences.
resources.resources: 1. Selected passages with new vocabulary reflecting certain fields e.g. marriage, family, health, sports. 2. List of new words from the passage. 3. Course book. 4. Dictionary

Use of Idiomatic Expressions: - Idioms expressed by phrasal verbs i.e. idiomatic use of languages as opposed to the literal use, e.g. My friend came round ten minutes after he had fainted; My friend came round to see me. - Accepted idiomatic expressions e.g. “to blow one‟s trumpet (to boast)”; “To let the cat out of the bag (to reveal a secret)”; “To give a person a cold shoulder (to ignore him)”; (Note: Proverbs are not idioms).

Word Formation: Synonyms, Antonyms and homonyms: - Words that are similar in meaning (Synonyms) e.g. enemy/foe; surrounding/ environment. - Words that are opposite in meaning (Antonyms) e.g. hot/cold, enemy/friend, long/short etc. - Homonyms: words with the same spelling but different meanings and sometimes different spellings.eg table /table; hare, hair

resources.title: Writing Biographies and Auto- Biographies
resources.description: Theme: WRITING PRIMARY 6 | Content: 1. Biography Writing: this is a form of descriptive writing which requires: - Close observation - Faithful recording of what was observed - description of the outside of the person being written about - Description of habits, manners, tasks, mental and moral qualities of the person - The life history, picking on the highlights of the history. 2. Auto-biography is a form of descriptive writing which requires: - Description of oneself, One‟s habits, tastes, manners, mental and moral qualities. - One‟s life history.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. Describe a person or thing so that everybody will readily recognize him or it. 2. Describe their teacher, a friend, a school, a favourite dog, a hoe or cutlass, their house. 3. Observe closely. 4. Write their own life histories.

Reads a passage on a life history of a person of note written by the same person. 7. Discusses the similarities and differences between biography and auto- biography. 8. Guides pupils to discover the techniques of writing a good auto-biographies.

Students: 1. Discuss the teacher‟s description of the boy. 2. Write the introductory paragraph about the person chosen. 3. Discuss the qualities with the teacher. 4. Listen to teacher‟s reading on auto- biography. 5. Tell the similarities and differences. 6. Find out their life history from their parents. 7. Write their own auto-biography.

resources.resources: 1. Course book 2. Flash cards 3. Charts showing synonyms and antonyms 4. Dictionary.
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. list the synonyms and antonyms of given words; and 2. use the words in sentences correctly.

resources.title: Review of Verb forms
resources.description: Theme: GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY PRIMARY 6 | Content: 1. Review of verb forms e.g. - tell, tells, telling, told - eat, eats, eating, ate, eaten.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. differentiate types of verb in relation to time; and 2. use the various verb forms previously learnt.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Gives examples using appropriate verb forms. 2. Encourages pupils to give more examples.

Students: 1. Write the examples given by teacher. 2. Give more examples of their own verb forms. 3. Use verb forms in sentences.
resources.resources: 1. Word cards 2. Flash cards 3. Course book
resources.assessment: Pupils to use the appropriate verb forms in sentences.

resources.title: Review of Direct and Indirect Speech
resources.description: Theme: GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY PRIMARY 6 | Content: 1. Direct speech e.g. “My mother gave me a book yesterday”, Tina said. 3. Indirect speech e.g. Tina said that her mother gave her a book the previous day.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. use indirect reporting orally and in writing; and 2. recognize the changes that take place in direct speech to reported or indirect speech.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Creates a true to life situation in which the language activity will take place 2. Guides pupils to use direct and indirect speech.

Students: 1. Practice use of direct and indirect speech 2. Dramatize the situation involving direct and indirect speech in groups.
resources.resources: 1. Chalkboard 2. Flash cards 3. Course book
resources.assessment: Pupils to use indirect reporting orally and in writing.

resources.title: Similes and Metaphors.
resources.description: Theme: GRAMMATICAL ACCURACY PRIMARY 6 | Content: Similes and Metaphors: 1. Use of comparisons ii. Similes and metaphors are best taught together, one helps to make the meaning of the other clearer, e.g. – she is as red as a rose. - she is a red rose.
resources.objectives: Pupils should be able to: 1. compare two things in respect of what they share in common; and 2. use similes and be able to turn them into metaphors and vice versa.
resources.activities:
Teacher: 1. Uses the blackboard work from which pupils will prepare their own list. 2. Encourages pupils to begin to look for these similes and metaphors in their extensive reading.

Students: 1. Construct sentences with similes 2. Make their own list of similes and metaphors. 3. Turn the similes into metaphors. 4. Prepare new similes, (this should be the joint effort of the pupils and the teacher).
resources.resources: 1. Flash cards 2. Course book 3. Sentence strips
resources.assessment: Pupils to: 1. compare things in respect of what any share in common; 2. identify similes and metaphors in sentences; and 3. use similes and metaphors correctly.
